transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-09-07 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Jordan Miles, Priya Raman, Alex Chen (Redwood) -- Lena Ortiz, Mark Hsu, Priya Banerjee, Evan Diaz (QuantumForge)

Summary (auto): Quick intro; alignment on staging infra and security; pilot scope defined; next steps and action owners.

[00:00] Jordan Miles: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um I'm Jordan from Redwood, i'll kick it off. can folks quickly say hi and role?
[00:12] Lena Ortiz: hey this is lena, CTO at QuantumForge. happy to be here.
[00:16] Mark Hsu: Mark, infra. we're standing up staging for the pilot this week.
[00:20] Priya Banerjee: Priya, product, focused on evals and UX metrics.
[00:24] Evan Diaz: Evan, security. i'll be the compliance POC.
[00:28] Priya Raman: Priya R from Redwood, solutions eng — i'll lead the technical handoff and run the perf checks.
[00:33] Alex Chen: Alex, CSM, i'll coordinate onboarding cadence and docs.
[00:38] Jordan Miles: great, quick agenda: network and access, KMS/encryption, pilot success metrics, rollout plan, then Q&A.
[00:47] Lena Ortiz: sounds good. our big blockers are network isolation and key management — we need to know whether we can keep keys in our KMS and still use Redwood private deployment.
[00:57] Priya Raman: yep so we have two main models: Hosted with customer-managed KMS via a federated key flow, or Private (VPC/on-prem) where the control plane sits in your VPC. both support BYOK but the integration steps differ.
[01:14] Mark Hsu: can you outline the network patterns? we're leaning away from public egress in staging.
[01:22] Priya Raman: sure — options: 1) VPC peering + private endpoints, 2) IPsec site-to-site for on-prem, 3) Transit gateway for multi-region. for staging minimal we recommend a private endpoint and limited CIDR allowlist. we'll send a checklist.
[01:40] Lena Ortiz: okay that matches our expectations. what about audit logs — we need immutable logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[01:49] Alex Chen: Redwood can forward audit logs to S3 or to your SIEM via syslog/forwarder; retention tiers are configurable. we'll include the recommended pipeline in the runbook.
[02:02] Evan Diaz: SOC2 stuff — do you have a standard controls list? we need to map Redwood controls to our audit.
[02:09] Jordan Miles: yes, we have a SOC2 matrix. i'll attach the controls mapping. also we support SAML SSO for admin accounts and RBAC for token scoping.
[02:20] Priya Banerjee: for the pilot, our success metrics are a) 95th latency under 350ms for small prompts b) cost per 1k tokens under $X (placeholder) c) hallucination rate below current baseline.
[02:34] Priya Raman: good, for latency we recommend Dedicated if you need strict SLOs. for pilot we can start Hosted with pinned capacity and fallback to dedicated if the perf variance is high.
[02:46] Mark Hsu: pricing tradeoff talk — what are ramp patterns for dedicated? we may need burst capacity.
[02:53] Jordan Miles: Dedicated is a reserved pool; we can configure burst buffers and autoscale policy. pricing addendum will show cost vs committed hours.
[03:04] Lena Ortiz: timeline: we want pilot in staging by Sep 15 and customer-facing beta Oct 1. feasible?
[03:11] Priya Raman: doable. main gating: staging subnet and KMS access. if we get those in this week we can run perf checks next week.
[03:21] Alex Chen: i'll coordinate the calendar invites and the onboarding ticket in our portal.
[03:26] Jordan Miles: ok let's dig into the access pattern. Mark, what access can you provision?
[03:31] Mark Hsu: we can stand up a test subnet in us-west-2 and r53 private hosted zone. no public NAT. we can allow Redwood egress IPs or set up a private endpoint.
[03:41] Priya Raman: private endpoint is preferred; it'll avoid public egress. we'll provide the ENI specs and the IP ranges.
[03:49] Mark Hsu: cool. we'll need the CIDR and port list.
[03:53] Priya Raman: will send. also for KMS: do you want to hold keys in AWS KMS or a separate HSM?
[03:59] Evan Diaz: prefer AWS KMS with a customer-managed CMK and external key policy so we maintain control.
[04:07] Priya Raman: supported. Redwood's KeyWrap flow lets you keep the CMK; we'll provide the minimal IAM policy.
[04:15] Lena Ortiz: any latency penalty for WRAPPED keys?
[04:19] Priya Raman: negligible; crypto handshake happens in setup and not per token.
[04:24] Jordan Miles: now onto observability — what dashboards do you need?
[04:30] Priya Banerjee: token-level cost, per-route latency histogram, error rates, and sample outputs flagged for quality.
[04:37] Alex Chen: those are standard; Redwood Console supports token breakdown and per-model tracing. we can give a demo of tracing in the canary.
[04:45] Jordan Miles: quick demo request — Priya R can you run a small batch sizing test and share numbers?
[04:50] Priya Raman: yes i'll run on the test model with 8 GPUs and send results. expectation: batching reduces per-token cost by ~20-40% depending on seq length.
[04:59] Mark Hsu: any special ports for KV cache?
[05:03] Priya Raman: KV cache is internal to the runtime; no external ports. just ensure low-latency network between app and endpoint.
[05:09] Lena Ortiz: regarding RBAC and environment isolation, can we scope tokens to only inference and not model management?
[05:16] Jordan Miles: yes, tokens can be scoped. admin roles can be limited to your SSO group.
[05:22] Evan Diaz: data residency — we need all inference to stay in us-west-2 for pilot. possible?
[05:27] Priya Raman: yes you can pin region; we'll route requests to that region only. we also support region-level fallbacks but you can opt-out.
[05:36] Priya Banerjee: about the pilot dataset, we plan to run three prompt suites: customer support transcripts, product docs Q&A, and config generation. we'll share a sanitized sample.
[05:47] Jordan Miles: good. we'll tie quality alerts to those prompt sets.
[05:51] Alex Chen: action: we'll create an eval set in the portal and set up regression alerts.
[05:58] Mark Hsu: how do we do rollouts? canary percentages?
[06:02] Priya Raman: rollouts support canary, A/B, and automatic fallback — e.g., start at 1% traffic, then 10%, etc. automatic rollback on increased latency or error rates.
[06:13] Lena Ortiz: team sync frequency? we want weekly check-ins during the ramp.
[06:17] Alex Chen: weekly works, i'll schedule a 30-minute cadence.
[06:21] Jordan Miles: budget constraints — any immediate blockers?
[06:24] Mark Hsu: just procurement sign-off; legal needs the standard DPA and security addendum.
[06:30] Jordan Miles: we'll surface DPA and the security pack.
[06:33] Evan Diaz: can you provide a diagram of where logs go and who has access? details matter for our auditors.
[06:40] Alex Chen: yes will include in doc pack.
[06:43] Priya Banerjee: curious about model upgrades in pilot — how are rollouts handled across model versions?
[06:50] Priya Raman: model versions are pinned per route. you can define rollout policies per-version and schedule. we also provide compatibility checks to avoid KV cache mismatches.
[06:58] Lena Ortiz: any recommended quantization for our use-case? we're sensitive to latency but also need quality.
[07:05] Priya Raman: suggest 8-bit quant for dev tests; for prod, test 4-bit quant profiles if quality holds. Redwood Optimize will give a recommendation based on your evals.
[07:16] Mark Hsu: for the demo can we see a side-by-side latency/cost tradeoff?
[07:21] Jordan Miles: yes we'll prepare a small spreadsheet with estimated unit economics per configuration.
[07:27] Priya Banerjee: integration: our app is on Kubernetes, is there a quickstart?
[07:31] Alex Chen: yes, SDKs for k8s, a helm chart, and example ingress config; link will be in the runbook.
[07:38] Jordan Miles: okay let's capture owners and dates. Alex, you'll own scheduling and doc pack?
[07:43] Alex Chen: yes I'll own that.
[07:45] Jordan Miles: Priya R you'll run perf tests and batch-sizing demo?
[07:49] Priya Raman: yes.
[07:51] Jordan Miles: Mark you'll provision subnet and KMS policy?
[07:55] Mark Hsu: yes.
[07:56] Evan Diaz: i'll confirm compliance docs to share.
[07:59] Jordan Miles: great. any more questions?
[08:02] Lena Ortiz: one more — will we be able to replay inference logs for debugging?
[08:07] Priya Raman: yes we can stream request/response samples to a secure bucket; PII must be sanitized per our shared guidelines.
[08:16] Priya Banerjee: note: we'll sanitize sample transcripts before sharing.
[08:19] Jordan Miles: perfect. wrapping up with recap and next steps.
[08:23] Alex Chen: recap: Redwood to share runbook, network checklist, SOC2 controls matrix, demo spreadsheet; QuantumForge to provision staging subnet, KMS key, and share QPS/latency targets.
[08:35] Jordan Miles: agreed. schedule: perf tests next week, canary demo Sep 14, pilot start Sep 15.
[08:43] Priya Raman: i'll post the perf results and the batch sizing notes.
[08:47] Mark Hsu: we'll send the subnet CIDR by tomorrow.
[08:51] Evan Diaz: i'll upload a list of compliance questions to the portal by Friday.
[08:56] Jordan Miles: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the doc pack and invite. bye.
[09:00] (call end)

Notes: Links shared during call: onboarding-runbook.pdf (link in portal), security-controls-matrix.xlsx (share in portal), canary-demo-invite (calendar). The transcript contains occasional mis-hearings and short overlaps typical of automated captions.
